screens.name: Today's runs
screens.purpose: Lists the driver's stops for the day in drive order with the status and delivery window of each.

screens.name: Stop detail
screens.purpose: Shows one stop: address, parcels, customer instructions and phone, with buttons to call, navigate and start proof of delivery.

screens.name: Proof of delivery
screens.purpose: Captures the photo, recipient name and signature that mark a stop as delivered.

screens.name: Failed delivery
screens.purpose: Records why a stop could not be delivered and marks the attempt as failed.

screens.name: Reassign stop
screens.purpose: Lets a supervisor move a stop from one driver to another with a reason.

screens.name: End of day summary
screens.purpose: Shows the day's delivered, failed and pending counts, cash collected and mileage, and lets the driver submit the day.

fields.label: Time window
fields.notes: The slot promised to the customer. Shown in red on stops 3 and 5 (11:00 – 13:00 and 13:00 – 15:00); the expert does not know why.

fields.label: Status chip
fields.notes: Values seen: DELIVERED, NEXT, PENDING. Expert also names failed.

fields.label: Time window
fields.notes: Shown in red on this screen.

fields.label: Parcel value
fields.notes: Printed next to each parcel; second parcel shows £20.

fields.label: Hazardous tag
fields.notes: Orange tag on parcel HL-374232. The expert does not mention it.

fields.label: Instructions
fields.example_value: Side gate is open. Leave it in the porch if nobody answers.

fields.label: Phone
fields.notes: The expert says every stop has a phone number, but this stop shows none and the Call button is greyed out.

fields.label: Parcel photo
fields.notes: Taken with the Take photo button. Placeholder text before a photo exists.

fields.label: Recipient name
fields.notes: Placeholder 'Who took the parcel?'. Marked with a red asterisk.

fields.label: Signature
fields.notes: Drawn with a finger in the box; no asterisk shown. Hint text 'Sign here with a finger'.

fields.label: Reason
fields.notes: Options seen: Nobody home, Refused by recipient, Address not found, Access blocked, Parcel damaged. Expert: you have to pick one.

fields.label: Anything else the depot should know?
fields.notes: Free-text box, placeholder 'Type here'. Expert says most people leave it blank.

fields.label: Supervisor notice
fields.example_value: Supervisor only. Signed in as Elmi Gracombe (Supervisor).

fields.label: New driver
fields.notes: Each option shows how many stops the driver has left: Salia Corbrook 3, Fenel Rosby 5, Sanel Belford 6.

fields.label: Reason for reassigning
fields.example_value: Van off the road, moving the rest of the route.
fields.notes: Expert says the reason goes in the audit trail.

fields.label: Cash collected
fields.notes: Expert: for cash-on-delivery parcels; the figure comes from finance.

fields.label: Mileage
fields.notes: Shown in a boxed input; expert says the driver types it in.

actions.description: Taps a stop in the list to open it
Presses Call to ring the customer
Presses Navigate to open the map
Presses Proof of delivery when at the door
Presses Take photo to photograph the parcel
Types the name of whoever took the parcel
Has the recipient sign in the box with a finger
Presses Delivered once it has turned green
Taps 'Can't deliver? Report a failed delivery' link
Picks one reason from the list
Optionally types extra information for the depot
Picks the new driver from the list

journey.description: After signing in, the driver lands on Today's runs and sees the six stops in drive order with status chips and time windows.
The driver taps a stop and reviews address, parcels, instructions and phone; can call the customer or open the map.
At the door, the driver presses Proof of delivery.
The driver takes a photo, enters the recipient name and gets a signature, then presses Delivered.
If nobody can take the parcel, the driver reports a failed delivery instead and picks a reason.
If a van breaks down, a supervisor reassigns the stop to another driver and records a reason.
At the end of the day the driver checks the totals, types the mileage and submits the day.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must, after sign-in, open on Today's runs showing the driver's six stops in the order they should be driven.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: When you sign in you land on Today's runs, which is your six stops in the order we'd like you to drive them.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show each stop with a status chip that is one of next, pending, delivered or failed.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Each stop has a little chip saying where it's at: next, pending, delivered or failed.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show under each stop's address the time window promised to the customer.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Under the address there's a time window, the slot we promised the customer.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must open the Stop detail page when the driver taps a stop on Today's runs.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Tap any stop to open it.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show on Stop detail the address, the number of parcels and any instructions the customer left.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You get the address, how many parcels are going there, and any instructions the customer left, like ring twice or leave it round the back.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a driver, I need a Call button on Stop detail that rings the customer, so that I can ring ahead if I am running late.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Call rings the customer and Navigate opens the map.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a driver, I need a Navigate button on Stop detail that opens the map, so that I can find the address.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Call rings the customer and Navigate opens the map.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must print the value next to each parcel on Stop detail.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The value is printed next to each parcel so you can see straight away.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must require both a photo and a signature to deliver a parcel worth more than one hundred pounds, with no exceptions.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Parcels over one hundred pounds need a photo and a signature, no exceptions.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must offer a Proof of delivery button on Stop detail that starts the delivery proof for the stop.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: When you're at the door, hit Proof of delivery.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must let the driver take a photo of the parcel on Proof of delivery.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: On Proof of delivery you take a photo of the parcel

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must let the driver type the name of whoever took the parcel on Proof of delivery.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: type in the name of whoever took it

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must let the recipient sign with a finger in the signature box on Proof of delivery.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: get them to sign in the box with their finger.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must keep the Delivered button grey and unusable until the photo has been taken, then turn it green and usable.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: See the Delivered button? It stays grey until the photo is taken. Once the photo is in, it goes green and you can press it.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must only mark a stop as delivered through the Delivered button on Proof of delivery.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: That's the only way a stop ever becomes delivered.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a driver, I need a link on Proof of delivery to report a failed delivery, so that a stop nobody answers is recorded rather than left on the step.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: And if nobody's in, don't just leave it on the step. Tap the link at the bottom to report a failed delivery instead.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must require the driver to pick one reason on Failed delivery before continuing.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You have to pick one, it won't let you carry on without.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must offer these reasons on Failed delivery: nobody home, refused, address not found, access blocked, damaged.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You pick a reason from the list: nobody home, refused, address not found, access blocked, or damaged.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must give an optional free-text box on Failed delivery for anything else the depot should know.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: There's a free-text box underneath for anything else, but honestly most people leave it blank.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must return a stop to the depot automatically after three failed attempts and drop it from the driver's list, with no action from the driver.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Three failed attempts and it goes back to the depot automatically. You don't do anything, the stop just drops off your list.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must allow only supervisors to reassign a stop.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: Only supervisors can reassign a stop.

requirement_candidates.statement: As a supervisor, I need to pick the new driver from a list when reassigning a stop, so that a stranded route can be covered.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You pick the new driver from the list

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must require a written reason when a supervisor reassigns a stop.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: you have to write a reason

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must record the reassignment reason in the audit trail.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: because it goes in the audit trail.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show on End of day summary how many stops the driver delivered.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: It shows how many you delivered

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show on End of day summary how many stops failed.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: how many failed

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must show on End of day summary the cash collected on cash-on-delivery parcels.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: and the cash collected, that's for the cash-on-delivery parcels.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must take the cash collected figure from finance and show it to the driver as given.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: The cash figure comes from somewhere in finance, I just take whatever it shows.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must let the driver type in their mileage on End of day summary.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You type your mileage in and press Submit day.

requirement_candidates.statement: The system must not allow Submit day until every stop is either delivered or failed.
requirement_candidates.source_quote: You can't submit until every stop is either delivered or failed, so check nothing's still pending.

questions.question: What makes a time window turn red on Today's runs and Stop detail (stops 3 and 5 are red in the recording), and what should the driver do when it is red?
questions.why_it_matters: A developer cannot build the colour rule, and the expert admits he does not know it.
questions.context_quote: The window shows red sometimes and I never worked out why, so I don't know what to tell you, just try to be there.

questions.question: Who or what decides the order of the stops and which stop is Next, and can the driver change the order?
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether the order is fixed by dispatch or something the driver controls.
questions.context_quote: your six stops in the order we'd like you to drive them

questions.question: What should the Call button do when a stop has no phone number? Stop 3 shows 'No number on file' with Call greyed out, yet every stop is said to have a number.
questions.why_it_matters: The expert's statement and the screen disagree, so the rule for a missing number is unknown.
questions.context_quote: Every stop has a phone number on it, so you can always ring ahead if you're running late.

questions.question: Is the one-hundred-pound threshold measured per parcel or on the stop total, and does a parcel of exactly one hundred pounds need a photo and signature?
questions.why_it_matters: Stop 3 has parcels worth £200 and £20, so the two readings give different results; the boundary value is also unclear.
questions.context_quote: Parcels over one hundred pounds need a photo and a signature, no exceptions.

questions.question: What does each parcel's HAZARDOUS tag mean for the driver, and does it change how the parcel is delivered or reassigned?
questions.why_it_matters: The tag is on screen but not explained; any handling rule attached to it is unknown.

questions.question: What must be complete before Delivered turns green: only the photo, or also the recipient name and, for parcels over one hundred pounds, the signature? The screen marks only Recipient name as required and says 'Take a photo to continue'.
questions.why_it_matters: The expert says the photo alone unlocks the button but also says over-£100 parcels need a signature; the two rules conflict.
questions.context_quote: It stays grey until the photo is taken. Once the photo is in, it goes green and you can press it.

questions.question: Is one photo and one signature taken for the whole stop or one per parcel? The screen header reads 'HL-387835 and 1 more'.
questions.why_it_matters: Decides how many proofs are stored when a stop has several parcels.
questions.context_quote: you take a photo of the parcel, type in the name of whoever took it, and get them to sign in the box with their finger.

questions.question: Is the list of five failed-delivery reasons the complete list, and does any reason trigger different handling by the depot?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert lists five reasons without saying it is the whole list.
questions.context_quote: You pick a reason from the list: nobody home, refused, address not found, access blocked, or damaged.

questions.question: In 'Last attempt: 01/05/2026', which date format is used, and why does it fall after the route date 01/04/2026 shown on Today's runs?
questions.why_it_matters: The attempt history date appears to be later than the day being worked, so the format or the data source is unclear.

questions.question: After a first or second failed attempt, what status does the stop show and does it stay on the driver's list to retry? After the third, is it counted as failed in the End of day summary?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert says the stop drops off the list on the third failure, yet Submit day needs every stop delivered or failed; the counts need a defined meaning.
questions.context_quote: Three failed attempts and it goes back to the depot automatically. You don't do anything, the stop just drops off your list.

questions.question: How does a supervisor reach Reassign stop, and what happens if a non-supervisor tries to open it?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert only says drivers 'won't normally see it', which does not define the access rule.
questions.context_quote: Reassign stop is a supervisor screen, so you won't normally see it.

questions.question: Does Reassign stop move one stop or a whole route? The screen works on Stop 3 only, but the expert talks about moving 'your stops'.
questions.why_it_matters: Decides whether a bulk reassignment is needed.
questions.context_quote: it's me or one of the other supervisors who moves your stops across to someone else.

questions.question: Which drivers appear in the New driver list, and is there any limit on how many stops a driver can take? Are the original and new drivers told of the move?
questions.why_it_matters: The list shows 'stops left' for each driver but no rule is given for who qualifies or how many is too many.
questions.context_quote: You pick the new driver from the list

questions.question: What exactly is stored in the audit trail for a reassignment (who, when, old and new driver, reason), who can read it, and for how long is it kept?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert names the audit trail but not its content or use.
questions.context_quote: because it goes in the audit trail.

questions.question: When is the cash collected figure supplied by finance, how does the system receive it, and what should the driver do if it does not match the cash actually held?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert does not know the source, so the integration and the discrepancy handling are undefined.
questions.context_quote: The cash figure comes from somewhere in finance, I just take whatever it shows.

questions.question: Is mileage required, in miles only, and what limits apply (minimum, maximum, decimals)? Is it trip distance or an odometer reading?
questions.why_it_matters: No validation rule for the mileage field was given.
questions.context_quote: You type your mileage in and press Submit day.

questions.question: What happens when the day is submitted: is it locked, who receives it, and what message does the driver get if a stop is still pending?
questions.why_it_matters: The expert stops at the button and gives no result or error behaviour.
questions.context_quote: You can't submit until every stop is either delivered or failed, so check nothing's still pending.
